generated.title: Excessive use of first-person singular 'I'
generated.description: The guideline explicitly states to avoid 'I' and to use 'we' sparingly, only for the thesis approach. The proposal uses 'I' 16 times across Sections 4, 5, and the AI Transparency Statement. The student should restructure these sentences to use 'we' (sparingly, for the thesis approach) or adopt an impersonal/third-person construction (e.g., 'The platform will be built…' or 'The thesis builds…').

locations.quote: **I will** build a platform on which any member of the chair requests time-limited access to any resource, a maintainer decides, and the access ends on its own. **I follow** the object-oriented software engineering method of Bruegge and Dutoit, and Figure 1 shows the actors and use cases of the platform as a use case diagram in the Unifed Modeling Language. **I pursue** four objectives:
**I will** replace the fat list of hosts and channels with a resource tree whose inner nodes are folders and whose leaves each carry a binding to one target system.
I will store the tree with a transitive-closure table of ancestor–descendant pairs and cap the fan-out, so that an approval on the root never reaches the whole infrastructure by accident.

**I will** defne one connector contract that validates a binding, grants and revokes access, and optionally lists the current members, and **I will** implement the keycloak-group, slack-channel, github-team, and webhook connectors on it.
**I will** build declarative request forms whose felds, visibility conditions, and rules turn answers into requests for a resource path, a level, and a duration.

**I will** therefore split the approval: in the review step, the resource owner records a decision without changing Keycloak, and in the grant step, the super admin sets membership and expiry atomically, in bulk for a vetted queue.
**I will** compare the manual administrative actions and the time to working access with the current process.
**I will** attach a recertifcation interval to each resource, which its descendants inherit, and open a campaign whenever the interval elapses.

The thesis runs from 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027, and **I divide** it into iterations of two to four weeks. Each iteration ends with an increment that a user can try in the web interface, and each item names the objective it serves and the outcome that **I demonstrate**.
Iteration 6 (18 February – 17 March), Objectives 2 and 3: webhook connector and deployment at the chair. Outcome: the correctness scenarios pass, and **I measure** the efort.
**I used** the following generative artifcial intelligence (AI) tool while preparing this proposal.
